sources.title: How to Visit the Great Mosque of Xi'an (by a Local Guide)
sources.content:
Great Mosque of Xi'an - Complete Information

Overview
The Great Mosque of Xi'an is situated in the Muslim community, approximately 300 meters from the Bell Tower. Originally constructed in 742 during the Tang Dynasty, it was rebuilt by Empress Cixi in 1900 and remains "the largest active mosque in Xi'an."

Historical Context
The mosque's origins trace to Arab merchants traveling the Silk Road who introduced Islam to the region. Intermarriage between these traders and Chinese populations led to the emergence of Chinese Muslims as a distinct community.

Visitor Information
Hours of Operation:
March to November: 9 am – 8 pm
December to February: 9 am – 6 pm

Admission Fees:
March to November: CNY 25 ($3.50 USD)
December to February: CNY 15 ($2 USD)

Visit Duration: 30–40 minutes recommended
Reservation: Not required

Architecture & Layout
The mosque features four courtyards with traditional Qing Dynasty symmetrical design:
1. First Courtyard: Contains the Imperial Hall housing "the only remaining Arabic stone tablet"
2. Second Courtyard: Features the Introspection Tower used for calling prayers
3. Third Courtyard: Houses the Phoenix Pavilion
4. Fourth Courtyard: Contains the main worship hall

Visiting Tips
Best Times: Visit after 10 am and before dark for optimal photography and access to surrounding shops.
Dress Code: Women should avoid camisoles, vests, shorts, or skirts. Non-Muslims cannot enter restricted prayer areas.

Nearby Attractions:
Huajue Lane (shopping and browsing)
Muslim Street (authentic Xi'an cuisine)
Bell Tower (300 meters away)
Gaojiadayuan (shadow puppet performances)

Transportation: Anticipate 15-30 minute walks from parking areas due to traffic restrictions.

sources.title: Great Mosque of Xian: Location, Ticket, Opening Hours & Travel Tips 2026/2027
sources.content:
Great Mosque of Xian: Location, Ticket, Opening Hours & Travel Tips

The Great Mosque of Xian in Huajuexiang, near Muslim Quarter, downtown Xian is the largest mosque of China where well preserved lots of ancient Chinese-Muslim style buildings.

Built in its present form during the Ming Dynasty, the Great Mosque of Xi'an is the largest and best preserved of the early mosques in China, and unlike most mosques in Middle Eastern or Arab countries, it is built mainly in Chinese architectural style.

The mosque is entirely different from other mosques, lacking the traditional dome characteristic of Arab architecture, so visitors may not immediately recognize it as a mosque upon entering. It mixes Islamic and Chinese designs.

The mosque features five courtyards, each feeling different and special. The first courtyard contains an elaborate wooden arch 9 meters high covered with glazed tiles that dates back to the 17th century.

The well-manicured gardens are filled with everything from standing rocks to white and pink magnolias, contributing to the mosque's tranquil atmosphere.

Tickets are ￥25.0 during busy season (Mar. to Nov.) and ￥15.0 during slack season (Dec. to Feb.) Most people spend 1 to 1.5 hours visiting.

Early morning or late afternoon is the recommended visiting time to avoid crowds and catch the best light for photos. Fridays get busy with worshippers, so weekdays are better for a calm visit.

sources.title: Xian Great Mosque: Facts, Travel Tips
sources.content:
Xi'an Great Mosque: Facts, Travel Tips

The Great Mosque in Huajue Lane is one of the oldest and largest mosques in China. Its architecture resembles a traditional Chinese garden rather than the typical Middle Eastern style, making it a unique stop to learn about Chinese Muslim culture.

The mosque was first built in 742 AD during the Tang Dynasty. Most of the visible structures date from the Ming Dynasty (1392 onwards). The mosque covers an area of 12,000 square meters.

The structure uniquely fuses Islamic and Chinese courtyard styles across five courtyards. Notable features include carved brick walls, a wooden gateway (pailou), and an octagonal meditation pavilion.

Location: No. 30 Huajue Lane, Lianhu District, Xi'an
Transportation: Walk north to the Drum Tower and then walk northwest along the Huajue Lane for around 5 minutes to reach the mosque.

Due to heavy traffic in the area, cars can only park nearby, requiring a 15- to 20-minute walk to reach the Great Mosque.

sources.title: Xi'an Great Mosque Travel Tips & Tours
sources.content:
Xi'an Great Mosque Travel Tips & Tours

The Great Mosque is located in the Muslim community, just 300 meters from the Bell Tower. It's best to visit the Great Mosque of Xi'an after 10 a.m. when the shops and restaurants in the Muslim Quarter and on Huajue Lane are open, so you can grab a bite to eat and explore this vibrant district.

Women are not allowed to wear camisoles, vests, shorts, or skirts, and if you are not Muslim, please do not attempt to enter the prayer hall and other areas that are not open to the public. During Muslim prayers, don't make noises and take pictures.

sources.title: 西安化觉巷清真大寺_百度百科
sources.content:
西安化觉巷清真大寺 - 内容提取

基本信息
中文名：西安化觉巷清真大寺
所属城市：陕西省西安市
地位：全国第三批重点文物保护单位

历史沿革
该寺院的建立和发展历程如下：
始建于明洪武年间(1368～1398)
成化二年(1466)进行重修
成化十八年(1482)奏请改寺名为"敕赐清修寺"
其后于嘉靖元年(1522)、万历三十四年(1606)和清乾隆三十年(1765)相继修葺扩建，遂成今日之规模

文化价值
原名为清修寺，因坐落在陕西省西安市化觉巷内，故名
是中国伊斯兰教著名清真寺
寺内曾设有经文大学，清代以来经学人才辈出，为经堂教育'陕西学派'的中心
现为全国重点文物保护单位

建筑特色
西安清真寺是一座中国古典建筑风格的建筑群，现存建筑基本以明代风格为主，整个建筑群分五进院落，属中国传统宫殿式建筑群，但在一些具体细节方面体现着伊斯兰建筑文化特点。

西安清真寺是西安地区现存规模最大、保存最完整的明代建筑群。作为伊斯兰教的清真大寺以其独特与古朴的建筑和园林景观在寺院园林中是比较典型的一个范例。

1988年1月13日，西安清真寺被中华人民共和国国务院公布为第三批全国重点文物保护单位。

sources.title: 西安化觉巷清真大寺游玩攻略 - 携程攻略
sources.content:
西安化觉巷清真大寺游玩攻略

基本信息
化觉巷清真大寺始建于唐天宝元年（公元742年），历经宋、元、明、清各代的维修保护，是一座历史悠久、规模宏大的中国宫殿式古建筑群。

门票价格
旺季（3月至11月）门票价格为25元，淡季（12月至次年2月）门票价格为15元。65岁以上老人免票。

开放时间与交通
开放时间：8:00-21:00
详细地址在陕西省西安市莲湖区北院门化觉巷30号，地铁/公交"钟楼"站下车可步行到达。

建筑特色
清真大寺融合了中国古典建筑风格和伊斯兰艺术风格，木雕、砖雕精美绝伦，处处体现中西合璧的美感。

参观建议
参观时注意尊重穆斯林宗教习俗；穆斯林一天需要做五次礼拜，每周五中午寺内还有主麻日大礼拜，这些时间寺内会有很多穆斯林，比较拥挤，但同时也是近距离接触穆斯林文化的好机会。

sources.title: Best Ways to Enjoy Xi'an Muslim Quarter and Great Mosque
sources.content:
Great Mosque Section from Muslim Quarter & Great Mosque Guide

The Great Mosque itself stands as China's oldest and largest mosque, with origins tracing to 742 AD, though most visible structures date from the Ming Dynasty (1392 onwards).

Great Mosque Architecture
The structure uniquely fuses Islamic and Chinese courtyard styles across five courtyards. Notable features include carved brick walls, a wooden gateway (pailou), and an octagonal meditation pavilion.

Visitor Guidelines
Essential etiquette includes:
Wearing modest, body-covering clothing
Removing shoes before prayer halls
Speaking quietly in sacred spaces
Respecting prayer times
Seeking permission before photography

Transportation
The Bell Tower station (metro) provides convenient access. Walking from Beiyuanmen through Hua Jue Lane leads directly to the mosque.
